correctness.rationale: An internal beat witness remains extremal after lexicographic substitution because every higher indexed fiber lies above every point of the current fiber, and dually below. Thus all chosen fiberwise beat deletions remain valid globally. After reduction, each core fiber is minimal and nontrivial, hence has neither a global minimum nor a global maximum. A hypothetical cross-fiber beat witness would force exactly such an extremum in one core fiber. The resulting lexicographic sum is therefore beat-point-free and is a core. A standalone verifier checks 352 finite constructions and 320 replayed beat deletions, plus the stated boundary example.

value.rationale: Lexicographic sum is a standard structural operation on posets. The theorem makes Stong-core computation compositional for arbitrary finite index posets when all fibers are noncontractible, reducing a potentially large global finite-space homotopy calculation to independent fiber reductions and giving an exact additive core-size invariant. The contractible-fiber counterexample shows that the hypothesis marks a real structural boundary rather than a cosmetic simplification.
